content.title: About
content.content: Green peas are young pods of the pea plant (Pisum sativum) harvested before the seeds fully mature. Raw peas have a fresh, slightly sweet flavor and a crisp texture. They can be eaten raw in salads, smoothies, or as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green peas belong to the legume family and are ancestors of many cultivated pea varieties used in cooking.
Raw pods are rich in B‑vitamins, especially folate, which is important for cell division.
In ancient cultures peas symbolized abundance and fertility.
Peas fix nitrogen in the soil, improving its fertility.
Raw green peas are common in Asian cuisines, such as Japanese and Korean dishes.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Raw green peas provide about 5 g of protein per 100 g, making them a good protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Peas are abundant in vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, iron, and magnesium, which are essential for immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Raw peas raise blood glucose slowly, beneficial for blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids in peas help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peas, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals; soaking peas before eating can mitigate this.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Legumes can cause increased gas and gastrointestinal discomfort in some people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw green peas can be tossed into fresh salads, blended into smoothies, added to salsas, or enjoyed as a crunchy snack after a brief blanching. They can also be soaked and sprouted for pea shoots.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store peas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze them in bags at –18 °C; thaw and rinse quickly before use.
